Welcome to Itchen Abbas Primary School!
Our school is a community; we would love you to be part of it.
Set in the heart of the Hampshire countryside, Itchen Abbas is a school where everyone knows everyone – from Year R right up to Year 6. It’s a school where children grow together in our classrooms, our woodland, our gardens and our dedicated outdoor learning space. It’s a school where wellbeing is always a priority, and where our personalised, inclusive approach builds confidence, develops curiosity and provides just the right level of challenge. We’re a true community school, offering the social and caring education every parent hopes for.
Looking for a New School?
We are offering tours with our Headteacher, Mr Bogan, to see the amazing facilities that we can offer you and your child. We have some spaces within our Year R and KS2 year groups for in-year transfers. Please call the school office on 01962 779310 to arrange an appointment.
If you would like more information or a tour of our school, please call the school office.

SEN (Special Educational Needs) & Inclusion
SENCO: Mrs Sarah Parsons
SEND Governor: Mrs Sharon Priest
Itchen Abbas Primary School is a mainstream Local Authority school. At Itchen Abbas, we are committed to ensuring equity for all our pupils. We aim to develop a culture of inclusion and diversity in which all are able to participate fully in the life of the school. We recognise that children make progress at different rates and not always in a steady linear pattern.
Children with SEND achieve well across the curriculum.
Inclusion Statement and Principles
Through high quality, inclusive teaching, we provide the right learning for the right child at the right time.
At Itchen Abbas, our community developed values underpin the inclusive culture and ethos of our school. Our values enable children to develop effective attitudes towards learning, strong learning behaviours and personal qualities. We teach our children to be reflective, resourceful learners with age-appropriate independence. Creativity is equally important to us, in the application of their learning and skills and as a means for self-expression. Developing respect and self-compassion enables children to form and maintain healthy relationships for others and themselves. We encapsulate these in our motto ‘Growing hearts and minds’ which is displayed in our Growing Tree.
​Our school ethos is one of encouraging success, progress and of building learning powers and high aspirations for every child. We achieve this through inclusive practice where adjustments and personalised learning facilitates equity of access and the right learning for every child at the right time. Inclusive practice is reflected in our school policies, responsive and relevant curriculum and high quality classroom practice.

Sports Premium
In 2013 the government announced that they would be spending £450 million over the next three academic years to help fund primary school sport, this is called the School Sport Premium. The PE and sport premium is designed to help primary schools improve the quality of the PE and sport activities they offer their pupils.
Schools have the freedom to spend the money however they choose, but this must be towards improving their provision of PE and Sport to give children the opportunity to develop a healthy lifestyle.
In the last few years we have improved our links with schools in our cluster to provide opportunities for competition in Netball, Football and Cricket. We hope to build on these relationships and increase our involvement in other competitions going forward.
We are very fortunate to have our very own sports coordinator, Mr Robbins, who teaches all classes across the week.
Stronger relationships with our local secondary school have enabled us to visit and make use of their purpose built Sports Hall and Gymnasium for specialised teaching sessions. We have plans to do this again in the future.

Pupil Premium
What is Pupil Premium?
The Pupil Premium is funding provided to schools which is additional to main school funding. It is allocated according to the number of pupils on-roll who are eligible for free school meals (FSM), a smaller amount allocated according to the number of children of service families, and an allocation for each pupil who has been ‘Looked After’ (in care) for 6 months or more. In 2012, funding was extended to include pupils who have been eligible for free school meals within the past 6 years.
The Government believes that the Pupil Premium is the best way to address the current underlying inequality in outcomes between children eligible for FSM and their wealthier peers, by ensuring that funding to tackle disadvantage reaches the pupils who need it most. However, it is for schools to decide how the Pupil Premium is spent, since they are best placed to assess what additional provision should be made for the individual pupils within their responsibility. Schools are to be held accountable for how they have used the additional funding to support pupils from low-income families and from September 2012, this information must be published.
Are you eligible for free school meals?
For every child registered, Itchen Abbas Primary School receives funding which enables us to provide additional resources, for example, new equipment and materials for pupils or provide extra classroom support. If you are registered for Free School Meals you could also get help with costs to support your child’s education and achievement. For example, the pupil premium can help fund the cost of school trips and extra-curricular activities.
Please register to make sure your child and others in their class and the school don’t miss out. No one will know you have registered and it will not affect any other benefits you are claiming.

Wraparound Care
We are proud to be able to offer Wraparound Care on-site at Itchen Abbas Primary School.
There will be 2 different offerings for wraparound:
8am - 8.30am - Breakfast Club. This will be charged at £4 a day and can be booked ad hoc or in advance using the booking form below. This will be charged to your SCOPAY account for payment.
3pm - 4/5pm - Wraparound Club. This will be charged at £6 an hour and must be booked in advance. (Advance means at least 3-days notice is required). You can sign your child up, using the booking form sent out each half-term, for one hour, both hours, on some weeks but not others – whenever it works for you. Children can also attend other clubs we offer (such as Interg8) and then join Mr Robbins for the second hour if you wish.
There is a limit of 13 children on Monday, Tuesday and Friday sports club and 15 on Wednesday and Thursday for LEGO & Computing. Mrs Goodwin is running an Art Club on a Thursday (limited to 13).
We will process your booking forms and set up a payment option for you on SCOPAY. Once payment has been received, Mrs Smith will email you to confirm that your child can attend Wraparound Club on the days/times you requested.
Please ensure you have read the Wraparound Policy and Children's Agreement below. It is important to read all sections, including late pick-up charges and what happens in the event of illness etc.
If you require wraparound provision for longer than 5pm (4pm on a Friday), please see below for more information.
Alternative Wraparound Providers
We also offer parents wraparound care through the use of external providers. We have a number of highly regarded child minders/nannies around Itchen Abbas who provide care for children before and after school. One of these providers is Debbie Collins who would be happy to chat about your childcare needs. She can be contacted on 07866514700 or deb.acollins@yahoo.co.uk. If you would like details of nannies in the area, please contact the school office for more information.
